newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: SOCCER-AFRICANS DELIGHTED AFTER HISTORIC 2-1 WIN OVER EUROPE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-AFRICANS DELIGHTED AFTER HISTORIC 2-1 WIN OVER EUROPE.

text.p: Africa's 2-1 win over Europe in the first ever All Star soccer match between the two continents was hailed as a symbolic victory by the African team manager and coach on Wednesday night.

Manager Mawade Wade of Senegal and coach Rabah Madjer of Algeria -- who scored Porto's winning goal when they won the European Cup in 1987 -- could hardly conceal their delight after the win at Benfica's Stadium of Light.

Wade said: "We wanted victory more than the European team and we deserved it. But it was not just a victory for the African team on the field. It was also a victory for the millions of Africans who were watching the match on television.

"Europe dominated Africa for many years and believed they were superior, but Europe now understands that things have changed between the two continents. We have the players and we have the talent, and we could put out 10 teams like the one we fielded tonight."
Madjer added: "We worked very hard for the victory, no-one handed it to us. I am very very proud and very happy for my players. The victory proved a lot tonight."

An outstanding 20-yard lob from African skipper Abedi Pele of Ghana after 14 minutes and a well-worked counter-attacking goal 12 minutes from time from Moroccan Mustapha Hadji -- who ironically plays for Benfica's arch-rivals Sporting Lisbon -- secured Africa's win.

Pele said afterwards: "This was a really important victory for Africa, which has shown the world that we can compete with the best and beat them. I am very happy about my goal, but more importantly I am very happy with the victory."

Europe's goal was scored by Frenchman Vincent Guerin after 44 minutes with a shot on the turn after German captain Juergen Klinsmann provided him with a delightful through ball inside a crowded penalty area.

Both sides had countless chances to add to their tallies in an open, attacking game which officially kicked off a new era in co-operation between the ruling bodies of European and African soccer and at the same time also launched the European Union's Year Against Racism.

But the match was watched by a disappointingly low crowd of less than 10,000 in the cavernous stadium which can hold 100,000. Heavy rain all day and the fact the match was being shown live on television in Portugal kept the numbers down.
It also did not help than many of Europe's top players -- including all those based in England where eight premier league matches were played on Wednesday night -- were not available for selection.

Rinus Michels of the Netherlands, who managed the European team, said he was very disappointed with the attendance, but added: "I was very impressed with the African team. They showed many of the artistic qualities they have on the ball, and, as a lover of the game, I appreciated their quick, sudden movements.
"I also thought that Abedi Pele was the outstanding player on the pitch, although I think in the second half we dominated the match and had plenty of chances to score."
The game was full of outstanding individual talent with players able to display many of their fancier tricks discouraged in more competitive club and international matches.
It was symbolically started by Eusebio, the greatest player in Benfica's history and the first African player to make any impact in Europe, back in the 1960s.
And although as a game it was rather disjointed as a spectacle, the fans that did brave the elements got their money's worth -- with the winning goal worthy of clinching any game.
Hadji, who was once selected for the French Under-21 side before electing to play for his native Morocco, began and ended the move, intercepting the ball in his own half.

He set up the counter-attack by running 40 yards before playing a one-two with Souleymane Sane then running on to take the return pass and cracking home a shot gave Russian goalkeeper Stanislav Cherchesov -- who had replaced Dutchman Edwin Van der Sar after an hour -- no chance.
Africa took the lead after 14 minutes when Abedi Pele somehow managed to lob Van der Sar, one of the tallest goalkeepers in the world.

The ball was worked from the back with a succession of crisp passes before being played out wide on the left to the Angolan forward Paulao. He picked out Pele on the edge of the penalty area and Pele picked his spot perfectly.

Europe had to wait until just before half-time for Guerin's equaliser and went close with an outstanding volley from Klinsmann after 38 minutes and a point-blank header from second-half substitute Pierluigi Casiraghi among others as play swung from end to end for most of the 90 minutes.
